headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from shared Dify datastore into gpt-engineer project files; no critical compliance signal.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can write uploaded knowledge-base content and shares state via the Dify server datastore, while gpt-engineer reads/writes a user project directory and consumes stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if Dify output is copied or surfaced into gpt-engineer, though no direct shared channel is documented. The pathway is real but not default-hijack critical.
conditions: IF Dify output is copied into gpt-engineer prompts or project files
IF the project directory contains attacker-controlled text that gpt-engineer treats as instructions
mitigations: Separate prompt/content files from executable project files
Add a manual review step before feeding Dify outputs into gpt-engineer
Use a read-only handoff directory for shared artifacts
Strip instruction-like text from retrieved knowledge-base content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and filesystem access, and Dify explicitly handles conversation logs, knowledge-base content, model-provider keys, and tool credentials. gpt-engineer touches generated source code in a per-project directory. If the same workspace or copied artifacts contain secrets, either agent can expose them through outbound model/API calls. The leak path exists in default-style use, but not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF secrets or conversation logs are placed in the shared project directory
IF either agent forwards file contents to its model backend or external tools
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project directory
Rotate any exposed API keys before pairing the agents
Restrict outbound network destinations where possible
Use separate workspaces for logs and code
requires-engineering: enforce secret-scanning before handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and spawn subprocesses, and Dify has per-conversation shared state via its datastore while gpt-engineer shares state via the project directory. If they operate on the same directory or mirrored artifacts, concurrent writes can overwrite code, prompts, or generated outputs without locking. The overlap is enough for irreversible corruption, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path
IF concurrent runs modify the same generated files without locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Serialize writes with a simple operator-run lock file
Snapshot the project directory before each run
Review diffs before accepting changes
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform that can wire tools into agent or workflow apps, and gpt-engineer writes files then offers to run generated code. If Dify-produced text or code is handed to gpt-engineer without verification, errors can cascade from prompt to code and then to execution. Because gpt-engineer can execute generated code with the user's privileges, the blast radius is potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF Dify output is used as authoritative input to gpt-engineer
IF gpt-engineer is allowed to run generated code without human review
mitigations: Require human review before code execution
Use Dify only for drafting, not final code generation
Disable auto-run of generated code
Test in a throwaway project directory first
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly touches conversation logs and knowledge-base content, while gpt-engineer touches generated source code. If regulated data is placed into Dify and then copied into gpt-engineer projects, retention and residency obligations can diverge across logs versus code artifacts. No specific jurisdiction or certification mismatch is documented, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in Dify conversation logs
IF the same regulated data is copied into gpt-engineer project files
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent
Set explicit retention limits for logs and projects
Delete stale conversation logs after use
Keep jurisdiction-sensitive data out of generated code
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy for the pair
